deep.reconstruction:
This folio is a working draft of passages of Riemann's Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (1851). The pieces correspond closely to Art. 6, Art. 13/14 and Art. 18 of the printed text. The page carries no computations, only statements and combinatorial or topological arguments.

(A) Top lines: end of a sentence on removable singularities. The condition is that the function (or its difference quotient) at a point ζ yields no discontinuity that could not be removed by altering values at isolated points. This is the setting of the Art. 13 theorem: a function of z that is continuous apart from isolated points and suitably bounded there has only removable discontinuities.

(B) Remark: if the domain of z is a multiply connected surface, the investigations need no essential change. This is followed by a deleted and rewritten sentence: 'From this, with the help of the theorem in Art. 13, one can conclude that in general, if in the interior at an isolated point of discontinuity [the function] becomes infinite ...'. This is the transition to the treatment of isolated singularities (poles and their order) in Art. 14.

(C) Proof of the Art. 6 lemma: each cross-cut (Querschnitt) q changes the number of boundary components by exactly ±1. There are three cases.
- Case 1: q joins a point of boundary component a to a point of a different component b. Then a, q, b, q (q traversed on both banks) form a single closed boundary curve. Two components become one.
- Case 2: q joins two points of the same component. Its endpoints split that component into two arcs, and each arc together with q closes up. One component becomes two.
- Case 3: q ends at one of its own earlier points. Then q = o ∪ l, with o a closed loop and l an arc from a point of o to a point of a boundary component a. Then o (one bank) and a, l, o, l form two closed boundary components. One becomes two.
Hence each cut changes the count by -1 (case 1) or +1 (cases 2 and 3), 'which gives the theorem to be proved'. In modern terms, the number of boundary curves after cutting along an arc changes by ±1. This underlies Riemann's connectivity count, i.e. the Euler characteristic bookkeeping of a bordered surface.

(D) Draft statement of the Dirichlet-principle theorem (printed Art. 18). The draft has two attempts; in the second, μ = u - α and ν = v - β. Let T be cut by cross-cuts into a simply connected T*. Let X+Yi (later α+βi) be a complex function of x, y with
Ω = ∫_T [(∂α/∂x - ∂β/∂y)^2 + (∂α/∂y + ∂β/∂x)^2] dT < ∞.
Then there is one and only one function u+vi of z, i.e. satisfying the Cauchy–Riemann equations u_x = v_y, u_y = -v_x, such that:
1) u - α = 0 on the boundary; v - β is prescribed at one point (fixing the additive constant).
2) The variations of u - α in T, and of v - β in T*, are discontinuous only at isolated points, and only so mildly that ∫((∂(u-α)/∂x)^2 + (∂(u-α)/∂y)^2) dT and the analogous integral for v - β stay finite over the whole surface. The latter function, v - β, has equal jumps on both banks of each cross-cut, so u is single-valued while v may have periods across the cuts.
The first attempt lists these as three conditions; the second merges finiteness into condition 2.

My addition: in the printed text the method minimises Ω over all admissible μ+νi with these properties. Writing α - μ = u, β - ν = v, the integrand of Ω for (α, β) splits as Ω(μ, ν) plus terms vanishing by Cauchy–Riemann. Existence then follows from Dirichlet's principle.
errors: No mathematical errors in the case analysis of (C); it matches the printed Art. 6 proof.
In (D) the draft writes '∫ ∂(u-β)/∂x' in places where (v-β) and ∂/∂y (squared) must be meant; this is a slip of the pen, corrected in the printed version.
Squares of the derivatives are not visibly written in the integrals of (D); finiteness of Dirichlet integrals (sums of squares) is clearly intended, as in the published Art. 18.
The existence part rests on the Dirichlet principle (existence of a minimiser), which is unjustified as Riemann used it; this is Weierstrass's 1870 criticism, later repaired by Hilbert (1900).

results.what: A cross-cut changes the number of boundary components of a surface by exactly ±1 (three-case proof)
results.modern_name: Effect of cutting a bordered surface along an arc on boundary components; connectivity / Euler characteristic bookkeeping

results.what: Isolated discontinuities that are suitably bounded are removable; consequences for isolated infinities
results.modern_name: Riemann removable singularity theorem; classification of isolated singularities

results.what: Existence and uniqueness of an analytic function on a cut multiply connected surface with prescribed real part on the boundary, with periods of the imaginary part across cross-cuts, via Dirichlet integrals
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle / existence of harmonic functions with prescribed boundary values and periods on bordered Riemann surfaces

deep.surprise_reason: These are drafts of passages of the published 1851 dissertation (Art. 6, 13-14, 18). The wording and arguments match the printed text closely. The page is of value for the genesis of the text but contains no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); f=exp(x)*cos(y); g=exp(x)*sin(y); simplify(diff(f,x)-diff(g,y)), simplify(diff(f,y)+diff(g,x))
checkable.asserts: Cauchy-Riemann for u+iv=exp(z): both expressions are 0, so the Dirichlet-type integrand vanishes for analytic functions.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); u=x**2-y**2; v=2*x*y; mu=Function('mu')(x,y); nu=Function('nu')(x,y); a=u+mu; b=v+nu; expand((diff(a,x)-diff(b,y))**2+(diff(a,y)+diff(b,x))**2 - ((diff(mu,x)-diff(nu,y))**2+(diff(mu,y)+diff(nu,x))**2))
checkable.asserts: Adding an analytic u+iv to mu+i*nu leaves the integrand of Omega unchanged (result 0). This is why the minimiser differs from alpha+i*beta by a function of z.
Cases 1, 2, 3 of the cross-cut lemma: the boundary count B goes to B-1, B+1, B+1, so it always changes by ±1.

transcription_corrections: Section D, condition 1 of the second version: 'v-β in keinem Punkte {+un+}stetig' should most likely read 'v-β in Einem Punkte gegeben', matching the printed 'ν in Einem Punkte beliebig gegeben'.
Section D, condition 2: 'mit Ausnahme einzelner Punkte {+un+}stetig' should read 'stetig' (stetig ändern), followed by 'und längs der Querschnitte von T auf beiden Seiten eine gleiche Änderung'.

In the line beginning 'Ist die Fläche T ...', the integral ∫∂X/∂x dT should be the Dirichlet-type integral ∫((∂X/∂x - ∂Y/∂y)^2 + (∂X/∂y + ∂Y/∂x)^2) dT. The phrase '{+wenn sie[?] nur und nur einer Function+}' is likely 'kann sie immer und nur auf eine Art in eine Function u+vi von z verwandelt werden, welche folgenden Bedingungen genügt'.

Top line 'ein Fortschreiten bei den Diff.-quot.' is uncertain; it is likely a phrase about the behaviour of the difference quotient at ζ, ending '... keine durch Abänderung in einzelnen Punkten hebbare Unstetigkeit ...'.
